text:
Mark Lazerus of The Athletic wrote this week that "Kyle Connor is going to be in the Hall of Fame someday," and added that he never seems to get the attention he deserves. Seventeen goals in 21 games won't fix that alone, but it helps. He ranks third among 529 skaters in our wins-added measure, behind only Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard.

The shooting is hot: 19% against 14% last season, on 12.2 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and our numbers expect some of that to come off. What's more striking is how much better the chances themselves are, 1.62 expected goals per 60 minutes against 1.02 a year ago. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking already had him in the 87th percentile for chances from right in front of the net. Luck is running the other way too: Winnipeg has scored 4.6 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him assists. In the first season after the Jets traded Connor Hellebuyck, Connor looks like a player worth more attention than he gets.
